candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 4 - boundary agreements and determined boundaries
verified_facts: The guide states that registered titles normally use general boundaries and that a determined boundary is used where a more precise boundary is required.
A determined-boundary plan must identify the exact line and surrounding detail and is normally drawn at a stated large scale.
semantic_limits: A general title-plan edge cannot be upgraded to exact legal-boundary evidence unless the determined-boundary evidence is actually present for the relevant title.

candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 5 - title plan
verified_facts: The title plan supports the property description in the register and graphically identifies the general extent of the registered land.
All title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary has been determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
semantic_limits: Title-plan red edging or graphical extent is not exact survey geometry by default and cannot silently raise parcel-area or height-result precision.
